claim: Store checklist, App Store 5.1.1(i): Link the privacy policy in App Store Connect and inside the app.
quote: All apps must include a link to their privacy policy in the App Store Connect metadata field and within the app in an easily accessible manner.

claim: Store checklist, App Store 5.1.1(i): Say in the policy how long you keep data and how users revoke consent or delete it.
quote: Explain its data retention/deletion policies and describe how a user can revoke consent and/or request deletion of the user’s data.

claim: Store checklist, App Store 5.1.1(ii): Get consent before collecting user or usage data.
quote: Apps that collect user or usage data must secure user consent for the collection, even if such data is considered to be anonymous at the time of or immediately following collection.

claim: Store checklist, App Store 5.1.1(ii): Write purpose strings that describe the whole use of the data.
quote: Ensure your purpose strings clearly and completely describe your use of the data.

claim: Store checklist, App Store 5.1.1(iii): Request only the data types the core features use.
quote: Apps should only request access to data relevant to the core functionality of the app and should only collect and use data that is required to accomplish the relevant task.

claim: Store checklist, App Store 5.1.1(v): Offer account deletion inside the app.
quote: If your app supports account creation, you must also offer account deletion within the app

claim: Store checklist, App Store 5.1.1(ix): Submit as the legal entity that provides a regulated healthcare service.
quote: Apps that provide services in highly regulated fields (such as banking and financial services, healthcare, gambling, legal cannabis use, air travel and crypto exchanges) or that require sensitive user information should be submitted by a legal entity that provides the services, and not by an individual developer.

claim: Store checklist, App Store 5.1.2(i): Disclose and get explicit permission before sharing personal data with a third-party AI.
quote: You must clearly disclose where personal data will be shared with third parties, including with third-party AI, and obtain explicit permission before doing so.

claim: Store checklist, App Store 5.1.2(vi): Keep HealthKit and camera-derived data out of marketing, advertising and data mining.
quote: Data gathered from the HomeKit API, HealthKit, Clinical Health Records API, MovementDisorder APIs, ClassKit or from depth and/or facial mapping tools (such as ARKit, Camera APIs, or Photo APIs) may not be used for marketing, advertising or use-based data mining, including by third parties.

claim: Store checklist, App Store 5.1.3(i): Use health and fitness data only to improve health management or for permitted research.
quote: Apps may not use or disclose to third parties data gathered in the health, fitness, and medical research context—including from the Clinical Health Records API, HealthKit API, Motion and Fitness, MovementDisorder APIs, or health-related human subject research—for advertising, marketing, or other use-based data mining purposes other than improving health management, or for the purpose of health research, and then only with permission.

claim: Store checklist, App Store 5.1.3(i): Disclose the specific health data you collect from the device.
quote: You must disclose the specific health data that you are collecting from the device.

claim: Store checklist, App Store 5.1.3(ii): Never write false data to HealthKit, and keep personal health information out of iCloud.
quote: Apps must not write false or inaccurate data into HealthKit or any other medical research or health management apps, and may not store personal health information in iCloud.

claim: Store checklist, App Store 5.1.3(iii): Get research consent that covers the five points Apple lists.
quote: Apps conducting health-related human subject research must obtain consent from participants or, in the case of minors, their parent or guardian.

claim: Store checklist, App Store 5.1.3(iv): Have ethics review board approval ready to show.
quote: Apps conducting health-related human subject research must secure approval from an independent ethics review board. Proof of such approval must be provided upon request.

claim: Store checklist, App Store 2.5.1: Use HealthKit for health and fitness, integrated with the Health app, and say so in the description.
quote: Apps should use APIs and frameworks for their intended purposes and indicate that integration in their app description. For example, the HomeKit framework should provide home automation services; and HealthKit should be used for health and fitness purposes and integrate with the Health app.

claim: Store checklist, App Store 1.4.1: Back every health-measurement accuracy claim with data and methodology.
quote: Apps must clearly disclose data and methodology to support accuracy claims relating to health measurements, and if the level of accuracy or methodology cannot be validated, we will reject your app.

claim: Store checklist, App Store 1.4.1: Remind users to check with a doctor before medical decisions.
quote: Apps should remind users to check with a doctor in addition to using the app and before making medical decisions.

claim: Store checklist, App Store 1.4.1: Attach your regulatory clearance documentation, if you have one.
quote: If your medical app has received regulatory clearance, please submit a link to that documentation with your app.

claim: Store checklist, App Store 2.5.18: No targeted or behavioral ads based on health data.
quote: may not engage in targeted or behavioral advertising based on sensitive user data such as health/medical data (such as from the HealthKit APIs)

claim: Store checklist, App Store 3.1.3(d): One-to-one live training may skip in-app purchase; group live sessions may not.
quote: One-to-few and one-to-many real-time services must use in-app purchase.

claim: Store checklist, Google Play Health apps: Console Declaration: Complete the Health apps declaration in Play Console.
quote: All developers must complete the Health apps declaration form on the App content page

claim: Store checklist, Google Play Health apps: Privacy Policy and Prominent Disclosure: Treat the app as a health app even if health is not its main purpose.
quote: If your app is not primarily a health app, but has health-related features and accesses health data, it is still in scope of the Health App policy.

claim: Store checklist, Google Play Health apps: Privacy Policy and Prominent Disclosure: Put the privacy policy link in Play Console and inside the app.
quote: Your app must post a privacy policy link in the designated field within Play Console, and a privacy policy link or text within the app itself.

claim: Store checklist, Google Play Health apps: Privacy Policy and Prominent Disclosure: Host the policy at a public, non-geofenced URL, not a PDF.
quote: Please make sure your privacy policy is available on an active, publicly accessible and non-geofenced URL (no PDFs) and is non-editable

claim: Store checklist, Google Play Health apps: Privacy Policy and Prominent Disclosure: Remove every permission the core function does not need.
quote: Permissions that are not required for a health app to perform its core functionality should not be requested and unused permissions must be removed.

claim: Store checklist, Google Play What permissions are in scope of the health apps policy?: Show a prominent disclosure and get affirmative consent for in-scope permissions (activity recognition, body sensors, Bluetooth, camera, location and others).
quote: If your app requires any of these permissions, it must prominently disclose how user data will be used, describe the type of data being accessed, and have the user provide affirmative consent for such use.

claim: Store checklist, Google Play Health apps: Health and Medical Functionalities: State the external hardware the medical function needs in the description.
quote: Apps that connect to external hardware or devices (e.g., blood glucose monitors) to perform their medical function, must clearly disclose these external hardware requirements in the app description.

claim: Store checklist, Google Play Health apps: Health and Medical Functionalities: List device compatibility for health functions that use the camera or other sensors.
quote: Apps that use device sensors (e.g., camera) for health functions must clearly state device compatibility information in the app description.

claim: Store checklist, Google Play Health apps: Health and Medical Functionalities: Declare a regulated medical device, and have proof of clearance ready.
quote: Apps that are regulated as a medical device must provide proof of approval, clearance or certification by the relevant authority upon request.

claim: Store checklist, Google Play Health apps: Health and Medical Functionalities: Otherwise, carry the not-a-medical-device disclaimer in the description.
quote: Other health and medical apps must include a clear disclaimer in their app description indicating that the app is “not a medical device and does not diagnose, treat, cure, or prevent any medical condition.”

claim: Store checklist, Google Play Health apps: Health and Medical Functionalities: Remind users to consult a healthcare professional.
quote: Apps must also remind users to consult a healthcare professional for medical advice, diagnosis, or treatment.

claim: Store checklist, Google Play Health apps: Additional requirements: Get informed consent and IRB or ethics approval for health research.
quote: Health Research apps should also secure approval from an Institutional Review Board (IRB) and/or equivalent independent ethics committee unless otherwise exempt.

claim: Store checklist, Google Play Payments - Clinical Services: Do not bill regulated clinical services through Play billing.
quote: Transactions involving regulated clinical services should not use Google Play’s billing system.

claim: Store checklist, Google Play User Data: Never sell personal and sensitive user data.
quote: Not sell personal and sensitive user data.

claim: Store checklist, Google Play User Data: Offer a way to delete the account and its data.
quote: Additionally, you must offer users a way to delete their accounts and associated data.

claim: Store checklist, Google Play Health Connect: publish guide: Complete the required Play Console steps: policies, Data safety, Health apps declaration.
quote: To get your health app published on Google Play, you must complete a few required steps in the Play Console.

claim: Store checklist, Google Play Health Connect: publish guide: Fill in the Data safety section.
quote: As part of your app publishing process, you must provide information for Google Play's Data safety section

claim: Store checklist, Google Play Health Connect: publish guide: Declare the Health Connect data types again whenever the set changes.
quote: This process must be completed for all publishing requests, both for a new app that has not been published yet, or when updating an existing, already published app that now uses a different set of data types.

claim: Store checklist, Google Play Health Connect: publish guide: Use the same privacy policy on the Play listing and in Health Connect.
quote: This must be the same privacy policy that is displayed to users when they click the privacy policy link in Health Connect

claim: Store checklist, Google Play Health Connect: Appropriate Access: Fit one of Health Connect's approved use cases.
quote: Approved use cases include: fitness and wellness, rewards, fitness coaching, corporate wellness, medical care, health research, and games.

claim: Store checklist, Google Play Health Connect: Minimum Scope: Request only the Health Connect permissions your features need.
quote: You must only request access to the permissions that are necessary to implementing your product's features or services.

claim: Store checklist, Google Play Health Connect: Limited Use: Never use Health Connect data to serve ads.
quote: Transferring, selling, or using user data for serving ads, including personalized or interest-based advertising.

claim: Store checklist, Google Play Health Connect: Limited Use: Never transfer or sell Health Connect data to ad platforms or data brokers.
quote: Transferring or selling user data to third parties like advertising platforms, data brokers, or any information resellers.

claim: Store checklist, Google Play Health Connect: Appropriate Access: No headless apps: the app needs a visible icon.
quote: Do not access data obtained through Health Connect using headless apps.

claim: Store checklist, Google Play Health Connect: Appropriate Access: Do not connect Health Connect to features that solely target children.
quote: Do not use Health Connect to connect to applications, services, or features that solely target children.

claim: Store checklist, Google Play Health Connect: Transparent and Accurate Notice: Publish help explaining how users manage and delete their data.
quote: User help documentation explaining how users can manage and delete their data from the app, and what happens to the data when an account is deactivated and/or deleted.

claim: Store checklist, Google Play Health Connect: Transparent and Accurate Notice: Say how you secure data, including HTTPS in transit.
quote: Information regarding handling all personal and sensitive user data securely, including transmitting it using modern cryptography (for example, over HTTPS).

claim: Privacy label helper, Apple: what "collect" means.
quote: “Collect” refers to transmitting data off the device in a way that allows you and/or your third-party partners to access it for a period longer than what is necessary to service the transmitted request in real time.

claim: Privacy label helper, Apple: third-party partners include SDKs.
quote: “Third-party partners” refers to analytics tools, advertising networks, third-party SDKs, or other external vendors whose code you’ve added to your app.

claim: Privacy label helper, Apple: identify all data you or your partners collect.
quote: You need to identify all of the data you or your third-party partners collect, unless the data meets all of the criteria for optional disclosure listed below.

claim: Privacy label helper, Apple: optional disclosure needs every criterion.
quote: Data types must meet all criteria in order to be considered optional for disclosure. If a data type collected by your app meets some, but not all, of the above criteria, it must be disclosed in App Store Connect.

claim: Privacy label helper, Apple: one optional-disclosure criterion is infrequent, optional collection.
quote: Collection of the data occurs only in infrequent cases that are not part of your app’s primary functionality, and which are optional for the user.

claim: Privacy label helper, Apple: ongoing collection after a permission request must be disclosed.
quote: For the purpose of clarity, data collected on an ongoing basis after an initial request for permission must be disclosed.

claim: Privacy label helper, Apple: data processed only on device is not collected.
quote: Data that is processed only on device is not “collected” and does not need to be disclosed in your answers. If you derive anything from that data and send it off device, the resulting data should be considered separately.

claim: Privacy label helper, Apple: data sent to service a request and not retained need not be disclosed.
quote: For example, if an authentication token or IP address is sent on a server call and not retained, or if data is sent to your servers then immediately discarded after servicing the request, you do not need to disclose this in your answers in App Store Connect.

claim: Privacy label helper, Apple: say whether each data type is linked to the user's identity.
quote: You’ll need to identify whether each data type is linked to the user’s identity (via their account, device, or other details) by you and/or your third-party partners.

claim: Privacy label helper, Apple: data is often linked unless de-identified before collection.
quote: Data collected from an app is often linked to the user’s identity, unless specific privacy protections are put in place before collection to de-identify or anonymize it

claim: Privacy label helper, Apple: personal data under privacy laws counts as linked.
quote: Note: “Personal Information” and “Personal Data”, as defined under relevant privacy laws, are considered linked to the user.

claim: Privacy label helper, Apple: what tracking means.
quote: “Tracking” refers to linking data collected from your app about a particular end-user or device, such as a user ID, device ID, or profile, with Third-Party Data for targeted advertising or advertising measurement purposes, or sharing data collected from your app about a particular end-user or device with a data broker.

claim: Privacy label helper, Apple data type Health & Fitness › Health.
quote: Health and medical data, including but not limited to data from the Clinical Health Records API, HealthKit API, Movement Disorder API, or health-related human subject research or any other user provided health or medical data

claim: Privacy label helper, Apple data type Health & Fitness › Fitness.
quote: Fitness and exercise data, including but not limited to the Motion and Fitness API

claim: Privacy label helper, Apple data type Sensitive Info.
quote: Such as racial or ethnic data, sexual orientation, pregnancy or childbirth information, disability, religious or philosophical beliefs, trade union membership, political opinion, genetic information, or biometric data

claim: Privacy label helper, Apple data type Location › Precise Location.
quote: Information that describes the location of a user or device with the same or greater resolution as a latitude and longitude with three or more decimal places

claim: Privacy label helper, Apple data type Location › Coarse Location.
quote: Information that describes the location of a user or device with lower resolution than a latitude and longitude with three or more decimal places, such as Approximate Location Services

claim: Privacy label helper, Apple data type Contact Info › Name.
quote: Such as first or last name

claim: Privacy label helper, Apple data type Contact Info › Email Address.
quote: Including but not limited to a hashed email address

claim: Privacy label helper, Apple data type Identifiers › User ID.
quote: Such as screen name, handle, account ID, assigned user ID, customer number, or other user- or account-level ID that can be used to identify a particular user or account

claim: Privacy label helper, Apple data type Identifiers › Device ID.
quote: Such as the device’s advertising identifier, or other device-level ID

claim: Privacy label helper, Apple data type User Content › Photos or Videos.
quote: The user’s photos or videos

claim: Privacy label helper, Apple data type User Content › Audio Data.
quote: The user’s voice or sound recordings

claim: Privacy label helper, Apple: in-app private messaging is declared as Emails or Text Messages.
quote: Declare emails or text messages on your label. Text messages refer to both SMS and non-SMS messages.

claim: Privacy label helper, Apple data type User Content › Other User Content.
quote: Any other user-generated content

claim: Privacy label helper, Apple: free-form text fields are Other User Content.
quote: Mark "Other User Content" to represent generic free form text fields and "Audio Data" for voice recordings.

claim: Privacy label helper, Apple data type Usage Data › Product Interaction.
quote: Such as app launches, taps, clicks, scrolling information, music listening data, video views, saved place in a game, video, or song, or other information about how the user interacts with the app

claim: Privacy label helper, Apple data type Diagnostics › Crash Data.
quote: Such as crash logs

claim: Privacy label helper, Apple data type Diagnostics › Performance Data.
quote: Such as launch time, hang rate, or energy use

claim: Privacy label helper, Apple data type Other Data › Other Data Types.
quote: Any other data types not mentioned

claim: Privacy label helper, Apple data type Purchases › Purchase History.
quote: An account’s or individual’s purchases or purchase tendencies

claim: Privacy label helper, Apple purpose Third-Party Advertising.
quote: Such as displaying third-party ads in your app, or sharing data with entities who display third-party ads

claim: Privacy label helper, Apple purpose Developer’s Advertising or Marketing.
quote: Such as displaying first-party ads in your app, sending marketing communications directly to your users, or sharing data with entities who will display your ads

claim: Privacy label helper, Apple purpose Analytics.
quote: Using data to evaluate user behavior, including to understand the effectiveness of existing product features, plan new features, or measure audience size or characteristics

claim: Privacy label helper, Apple purpose Product Personalization.
quote: Customizing what the user sees, such as a list of recommended products, posts, or suggestions

claim: Privacy label helper, Apple purpose App Functionality.
quote: Such as to authenticate the user, enable features, prevent fraud, implement security measures, ensure server up-time, minimize app crashes, improve scalability and performance, or perform customer support

claim: Privacy label helper, Apple purpose Other Purposes.
quote: Any other purposes not listed

claim: Privacy label helper, Google: what "collect" means.
quote: "Collect" means transmitting data from your app off a user’s device.

claim: Privacy label helper, Google: collection includes libraries and SDKs.
quote: Libraries and SDKs: This includes user data transmitted off device from your app by libraries and/or SDKs used in your app, irrespective of whether data is transmitted to you or a third-party server.

claim: Privacy label helper, Google: the declaration covers third-party libraries and SDKs.
quote: This includes data collected and handled through any third-party libraries or SDKs used in their apps.

claim: Privacy label helper, Google: apps that collect nothing still complete the form.
quote: Even developers with apps that do not collect any user data must complete this form and provide a link to their privacy policy.

claim: Privacy label helper, Google: on-device processing is not collection.
quote: On-device access/processing: User data accessed by your app that is only processed locally on the user’s device and not sent off device does not need to be disclosed.

claim: Privacy label helper, Google: ephemeral processing is in the form but not shown on the listing.
quote: Ephemeral processing: User data transmitted off device that is processed ephemerally needs to be included in your form response, but if it meets the standard below, it will not be disclosed in your app’s Data safety section on Google Play.

claim: Privacy label helper, Google: what ephemeral means.
quote: Processing data "ephemerally" means accessing and using it while the data is only stored in memory and retained for no longer than necessary to service the specific request in real-time.

claim: Privacy label helper, Google: building profiles is never ephemeral.
quote: However, using data to build advertising profiles or other user profiles cannot be treated as ephemeral and must be declared as collection or sharing for the relevant purposes.

claim: Privacy label helper, Google: pseudonymous data must be disclosed.
quote: Pseudonymous data: User data collected pseudonymously must be disclosed. For example, data that can reasonably be re-associated with a user must be disclosed.

claim: Privacy label helper, Google: what "sharing" means.
quote: "Sharing" refers to transferring user data collected from your app to a third party.

claim: Privacy label helper, Google: SDK transfers to third parties are sharing.
quote: From your app libraries and SDKs. Transferring data collected from your app off a user’s device directly to a third party via libraries and/or SDKs included in your app.

claim: Privacy label helper, Google: transfers to service providers are not sharing.
quote: Service providers. Transferring user data to a "service provider" that processes it on behalf of the developer.

claim: Privacy label helper, Google: user-initiated or consented transfers are not sharing.
quote: User-initiated action or prominent disclosure and user consent. Transferring user data to a third party based on a specific user-initiated action, where the user reasonably expects the data to be shared, or based on a prominent in-app disclosure and consent that meets the requirements described in our User Data policy

claim: Privacy label helper, Google: each data type is optional or required.
quote: You can also disclose whether each data type collected by your app is "optional" or "required." "Optional" includes the ability to opt into or opt out of data collection.

claim: Privacy label helper, Google: optional only if every user can choose.
quote: You can declare that your app collects certain data optionally only if all users – regardless of device or region – can either optionally provide information, opt-out, or opt-in to have the data collected.

claim: Privacy label helper, Google: data the primary functionality needs is required.
quote: If your app’s primary functionality requires the data type, you should declare that data as "required."

claim: Privacy label helper, Google data type Health and fitness › Health info.
quote: Information about a user's health, such as medical records or symptoms.

claim: Privacy label helper, Google data type Health and fitness › Fitness info.
quote: Information about a user's fitness, such as exercise or other physical activity.

claim: Privacy label helper, Google data type Location › Precise location.
quote: User or device physical location within an area less than 3 square kilometers, such as location provided by Android’s ACCESS_FINE_LOCATION permission.

claim: Privacy label helper, Google data type Location › Approximate location.
quote: User or device physical location to an area greater than or equal to 3 square kilometers, such as the city a user is in, or location provided by Android’s ACCESS_COARSE_LOCATION permission.

claim: Privacy label helper, Google data type Personal info › Name.
quote: How a user refers to themselves, such as their first or last name, or nickname.

claim: Privacy label helper, Google data type Personal info › Email address.
quote: A user’s email address.

claim: Privacy label helper, Google data type Personal info › User IDs.
quote: Identifiers that relate to an identifiable person. For example, an account ID, account number, or account name.

claim: Privacy label helper, Google data type Personal info › Other info.
quote: Any other personal information such as date of birth, gender identity, veteran status, etc.

claim: Privacy label helper, Google data type Device or other IDs.
quote: Identifiers that relate to an individual device, browser or app. For example, an IMEI number, MAC address, Widevine Device ID, Firebase installation ID, or advertising identifier.

claim: Privacy label helper, Google data type Photos and videos › Photos.
quote: A user’s photos.

claim: Privacy label helper, Google data type Photos and videos › Videos.
quote: A user’s videos.

claim: Privacy label helper, Google data type Audio files › Voice or sound recordings.
quote: A user’s voice such as a voicemail or a sound recording.

claim: Privacy label helper, Google data type Messages › Other in-app messages.
quote: Any other types of messages. For example, instant messages or chat content.

claim: Privacy label helper, Google data type App activity › Other user-generated content.
quote: Any other user-generated content not listed here, or in any other section. For example, user bios, notes, or open-ended responses.

claim: Privacy label helper, Google data type App activity › App interactions.
quote: Information about how a user interacts with the app. For example, the number of times they visit a page, screenshots taken, or sections they tap on.

claim: Privacy label helper, Google data type App info and performance › Crash logs.
quote: Crash log data from your app. For example, the number of times your app has crashed, stack traces, or other information directly related to a crash.

claim: Privacy label helper, Google data type App info and performance › Diagnostics.
quote: Information about the performance of your app. For example battery life, loading time, latency, framerate, or any technical diagnostics.

claim: Privacy label helper, Google data type Financial info › Purchase history.
quote: Information about purchases or transactions a user has made.

claim: Privacy label helper, Google purpose App functionality.
quote: Used for features that are available in the app

claim: Privacy label helper, Google purpose Analytics.
quote: Used to collect data about how users use the app or how it performs

claim: Privacy label helper, Google purpose Developer communications.
quote: Used to send news or notifications about the app or the developer.

claim: Privacy label helper, Google purpose Advertising or marketing.
quote: Used to display or target ads or marketing communications, or measuring ad performance

claim: Privacy label helper, Google purpose Fraud prevention, security, and compliance.
quote: Used for fraud prevention, security, or compliance with laws.

claim: Privacy label helper, Google purpose Personalization.
quote: Used to customize your app, such as showing recommended content or suggestions.

claim: Privacy label helper, Google purpose Account management.
quote: Used for the setup or management of a user’s account with the developer.
